topic: Smart Pointers for Automatic Memory Management
explanation:
Smart pointers in C++ are template classes that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation when objects go out of scope. They are used to prevent memory leaks and dangling pointers, promoting safer and more maintainable code by adhering to RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) principles. Modern C++ encourages replacing raw pointers with smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr for resource management.

Smart pointers in C++ (such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr) are template classes that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation when objects go out of scope. They are used to prevent memory leaks and dangling pointers, adhering to the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom. Modern C++ encourages their use over raw pointers for safer and more expressive resource management.
syntax:
std::unique_ptr<Type> ptr = std::make_unique<Type>(constructor_args); // for exclusive ownership
std::shared_ptr<Type> sptr = std::make_shared<Type>(constructor_args); // for shared ownership
